children: Earlier this week, the CEOs of Anthropic
, OpenAI
, and SpaceX
, along with senior executives at Microsoft
and Google
, voiced support for a temporary slow down in AI development while the sector grapples with safety issues associated with the technology.
We asked Seeking Alpha analysts
, and
which companies they thought would be most impacted by a deceleration in AI development.

Carla Magliocco: I don't have a totally clear understanding of what an AI slowdown means. If it is only regulation to supervise the development of AI, it doesn't worry me. But if it implies fewer language models and limits their massive adoption, evidently that could lead to a drop in hyperscalers' investment, among which I include Alphabet
, Meta Platforms
, Amazon
, Microsoft
, and Oracle

But these big companies wouldn't be the most affected. The companies that would be more impacted are those that still operate at a loss and depend on long-term deals to build complete data centers. Companies such as CoreWeave
, Hut 8 Corp.
, or IREN
could be the most affected. Nebius
, which I have held in my portfolio for a few weeks, could also drop sharply.
This pattern could repeat throughout the entire hardware supply chain. The whole semiconductor sector would fall, but shares like Marvell Technology
or Advanced Micro Devices
, which trade at 79 and 131 times their earnings, respectively, could, in my view, suffer more than more established companies such as Nvidia
or Broadcom

Shailja Sharma: The obvious answer is the AI supply chain, but I think that is not an accurate interpretation of what was actually said. There has never been any suggestion of slowing down inference, which is where the demand lies. Dell
predicts inference tokens growing 87 times by 2030 against training at roughly five.
Memory is where I would have the least concerns despite it getting sold the hardest following the news. Micron
, SK Hynix
, and Sandisk
all declined, but according to Nvidia's
own recent filing, supply commitments increased from $119B to $279B in just one quarter, mostly on memory. That is a contract, not a sentiment.
The truly exposed names are those levered to a few buyers. Broadcom
has guided fiscal 2027 AI revenue to around $115B, on programs with four customers. Credo
and Marvell
sit in the same category. The neoclouds, CoreWeave
and Nebius
, carry the capex and rent the capacity, so they feel it first.
The only thing that has actually changed is OpenAI
delaying its IPO. That is capital not raised by one of the biggest purchasers of compute. Everything else was words.
I would watch the hyperscaler capex guides rather than the essays.
JR Research: To be clear, if an AI slowdown were to happen, we are generally talking about training compute capacity getting stymied or AI data centers focusing on training compute getting impeded.

And since these could affect the frontier labs, the effects could percolate through the AI supply chain, as they are expected to be the largest source of compute revenue generation for the next few years.

They are trying to solve for the hardest models (in this case, the next stage leading to recursive self-improvement, or RSI for short) and have become front and center, whether in the U.S. or China. Therefore, it's pretty clear that RSI should be considered a significant leap, a step-function change in model capability, whoever gets there first.
If we were to focus on particular segments within the AI value chain, then possibly the neoclouds could be more exposed.
We already know that neoclouds like CoreWeave
and Nebius
are currently still highly dependent on the hyperscalers to convert that contracted backlog into connected power.

The second thing is that they are not expected to turn free cash flow positive through the rest of the decade. If they cannot scale their capacity quickly enough as conversion gets further delayed, then this could hurt their FCF growth inflection point even further, dragging out their margins profile.
Crypto miners like Iren
, who are trying to become a bigger cloud and a more dominant AI cloud, could also see ambitions getting hindered.
Essentially companies linked to the AI cloud or new cloud space will likely be more exposed to this challenge if it plays out subsequently.
(JR Research leads the SA investing group Ultimate Growth Investing.)

title: SA Asks: Which companies would be most impacted by an AI slowdown?
